quality.title: Quality check
quality.advisory: These are suggestions from fixed rules. They never stop you saving, and nothing is sent to an AI service.
quality.empty: Type the wording to see suggestions.
quality.unavailable: The quality check is not available right now. You can still save.

vague_verb.name: Vague verb
vague_verb.message: Vague verb: {{verbs}}. It is hard to observe or assess.
vague_verb.suggestion: Use a verb you can observe, such as explain, describe, demonstrate or calculate.

multiple_verbs.name: More than one verb
multiple_verbs.message: More than one verb: {{verbs}}. Each verb is a separate thing to teach and assess.
multiple_verbs.suggestion: Keep one verb here and write the others as separate objectives.

too_long.name: Too long
too_long.suggestion: Shorten it, or split it into separate objectives.

too_short.name: Very short
too_short.suggestion: Say what the learner does, and with what.

missing_upward_link.name: No upward link
missing_upward_link.message: It does not contribute to any broader outcome.
missing_upward_link.suggestion: Tick the outcomes it helps to achieve.

no_action_verb.name: No known verb
no_action_verb.message: It does not start with a verb the checker knows ("{{word}}").
no_action_verb.suggestion: Start with a measurable action verb, for example "Explain" or "Perform".

learner_framing.name: Lead-in wording
learner_framing.message: It starts with a lead-in such as "Students will be able to".
learner_framing.suggestion: Start with the verb. The lead-in can be shown once above the list.

ambiguous_qualifier.name: Hard-to-measure words
ambiguous_qualifier.message: Words that are hard to measure: {{words}}.
ambiguous_qualifier.suggestion: Say what counts as appropriate or well, for example how many or to what standard.

level_differs.name: Level differs from the verb
level_differs.message: The level chosen ({{chosen}}) differs from the level the verb "{{verb}}" usually points to ({{suggested}}).
level_differs.suggestion: Check the level, or keep it if the objective needs it.

near_duplicate.name: Near-duplicate
near_duplicate.message: Near-duplicate of an objective in {{where}} ({{percent}}% similar). Repeat on purpose, or remove?
near_duplicate.suggestion: Compare the two. Keep both if the repeat is on purpose; otherwise remove or reword one.

possible_personal_information.name: May hold personal information
possible_personal_information.message: The wording may hold personal information: {{kinds}}.
possible_personal_information.suggestion: Remove or generalise it. Objectives must not name or identify people, and never a patient.

help.title: Coverage and depth
help.text: Coverage: how much of this framework item the objective teaches, from 0 (none) to 5 (more than 80%). Depth: whether the objective asks students to work at the level the item expects (for example, knowing versus doing). Both affect the weighted coverage report.

outside.title: Text will be sent outside South Africa
outside.body: This provider processes the text it is sent outside South Africa. Only curriculum text (objectives, framework items, titles and descriptions) is sent, never personal information, but your information officer should know. Check the provider's terms for how it stores and uses what it receives.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: A privacy guard checks every message before it leaves. Only curriculum fields are allowed, and the text is scanned for email addresses, phone numbers, ID and student numbers, titles with names, and the names of this site's users.
privacy.localOnlyHelp: When on, only a provider on this server or network can be used. Providers anywhere else are blocked.
privacy.personalDataHelp: This applies to anything the guard finds in the text.
privacy.refuseHelp: Nothing is sent. The person is told what kind of information was found, not the text itself.
privacy.redact: Replace it with a placeholder and send the rest
privacy.redactHelp: The found text is swapped for a note such as [email removed], and the text is checked again before it is sent.

evaluation.title: Check the AI's mapping
evaluation.description: Mark the AI against an answer key that people wrote, and see how often they agree. Use the figures to choose the settings for AI suggestions and bulk accept.
evaluation.honest: They are only as good as the answer key. A gold set written by one person, or by the people who built the prompt, measures that person's view. These figures start from nothing: the AI is not shown earlier decisions, so a programme with reviewed links will do somewhat better. Kappa depends on how many items the AI was shown for each objective.
evaluation.loadErrorBody: Nothing was changed. Check your connection and try again.

gold.title: Gold sets
gold.intro: A gold set is a list of objectives with the framework items a person decided they map to. It is the answer key the AI is marked against. Fill it in by hand, without looking at what the AI suggested.
gold.none: No gold sets yet. Download the template below, fill it in, and add it here.
gold.name: Name
gold.addHelp: The template has one row for each objective and framework item: the objective's wording exactly as in the curriculum, the item code, the coverage (0 to 5) and the depth. An objective that maps to nothing gets one row with no code.
gold.summary: {{objectives}} objectives, {{mappings}} mappings, {{none}} objectives that map to nothing.
gold.problemsTitle: Nothing is saved until these are fixed

run.title: Run an evaluation
run.intro: The AI is asked to map the gold set's objectives, exactly as in a mapping run, but nothing is saved: no link is made and no objective changes. This calls the AI provider and costs money; the cost is shown with the result.
run.versionHelp: The objectives are found in this version by their wording. Objectives it does not have are left out.
run.started: The evaluation has started. Its figures appear below when it finishes.

results.title: Results
results.intro: Each row is one prompt version and model on one gold set. The figures are worked out from the AI's stored answers, so changing the minimum coverage does not cost anything.
results.minCoverage: Count suggestions with a coverage of
results.minCoverageHelp: The AI's own coverage score, 1 to 5. This is the setting for AI suggestions.
results.scoreKappaTitle: Weighted kappa on the coverage score of the links both made

detail.title: {{prompt}} on {{model}}
detail.counts: {{objectives}} objectives answered, {{failed}} the AI could not answer, {{missing}} not found in the version. The AI was shown {{shown}} items on average for each objective.
detail.coverageHelp: Precision: of the links the AI suggested, how many the gold set also has. Recall: of the links in the gold set, how many the AI suggested. Kappa: agreement beyond chance (0.6 is the target for a pilot). "Shown to the AI" is the share of gold links that were on the AI's shortlist at all; recall cannot be higher than that.
detail.bulkTitle: Bulk accept, with a minimum coverage of {{n}} or more
detail.bulkHelp: Bulk accept approves every suggestion whose confidence reaches the floor. "Wrong" counts accepted links that are not in the gold set. Choose the lowest floor whose precision you would accept for links nobody looks at.
detail.disagreeTitle: Where the AI and the gold set disagree
detail.noDisagreements: They agree on every objective at this setting.
detail.scoreKappaHelp: Coverage-score kappa is worked out on the links that both the AI and the gold set made, from the two coverage scores (0 to 5), with quadratic weights so that a near miss counts for little and a far miss for a lot. It is the kind of figure the study the owner cited reports between its two raters (0.68; Theurich et al. 2025), so it is the one to compare with that. It says nothing about which links exist: the other figures do. Read it with the number of links it is based on.
